rules.message: Word documented as over-represented in LLM output.
rules.fix: Replace with the plain or specific word (delve into -> examine/look at; underscore -> show; showcase -> show; pivotal -> important, or give the concrete consequence; testament to -> shows; boasts -> has). Better: replace the abstraction with the fact it gestures at.
rules.false_positive_notes: 'underscore' as the _ character or film score; 'realm' in fantasy/legal contexts; 'boasts' in sports copy. Wikipedia: treat literally, synonyms are not implicated.
examples_flagged: This study delves into the data.
It stands as a testament to her work.

rules.threshold: error if >=3 distinct EN-AI-001 lemmas per 300 words, or >=5 distinct EN-AI-001/003 lemmas per 300 words (heuristic, not from a source)
rules.message: Several distinct AI-vocabulary words co-occur; Wikipedia calls clustering 'one of the strongest tells'.
rules.fix: Rewrite the passage from the facts up rather than swapping synonyms one by one.

rules.pattern: \b(?:vibrant|seamless(?:ly)?|robust|leverag(?:e|es|ed|ing)|unlock(?:s|ed|ing)?|elevat(?:e|es|ed|ing)|empower(?:s|ed|ing|ment)?|foster(?:s|ed|ing)?|(?:evolving|ever-evolving|digital|competitive|business) landscape|holistic|cutting-edge|state-of-the-art|game-?chang(?:er|ing)|groundbreaking|revolutioni[sz](?:e|es|ed|ing)|renowned|nestled|in the heart of|diverse array|rich (?:cultural )?heritage|commitment to|streamlin(?:e|es|ed|ing)|synerg(?:y|ies)|best-in-class|world-class|transformative|navigat(?:e|ing) the complexities)\b
rules.message: Promotional/buzzword language (LLM puffery; GOV.UK 'words to avoid').
rules.fix: Say what the thing does, for whom, with a number or example. GOV.UK: leverage -> use/influence; empower -> allow; foster -> encourage/help; robust -> well thought out/comprehensive; streamline -> simplify.
rules.false_positive_notes: Literal uses (a 'vibrant' colour in a paint spec; 'foster' care; 'robust' physical object per GOV.UK exception).
examples_flagged: Nestled in the heart of the city.

rules.pattern: \b(?:stands as|serves as a (?:testament|reminder|symbol|beacon)|is a testament to|a testament to|plays? an? (?:vital|crucial|pivotal|key|significant|important|central) role|mark(?:s|ed|ing)? an? (?:pivotal|significant|key|major|important) (?:moment|shift|milestone|turning point)|setting the stage for|left an indelible mark|indelible mark|deeply rooted|enduring legacy|lasting legacy|reflects? (?:a )?broader|evolving landscape|key turning point|focal point|represents? a (?:significant )?shift)\b
rules.message: Undue emphasis on significance/legacy (Wikipedia 'words to watch').
rules.fix: Delete the sentence or replace it with the specific, sourced consequence (who changed what, when).
examples_flagged: It plays a vital role in the ecosystem.
The founding marked a pivotal moment.
examples_ok: The pump moves 40 litres a minute.

rules.message: Avoidance of 'is/are' (LLM pattern; one study found >10% drop in 'is/are' in 2023 academic text, per Wikipedia).
rules.fix: Use 'is/are/was' unless the role meaning is literal (e.g. 'she served as treasurer').
rules.false_positive_notes: Literal roles ('served as mayor 2010-2014') are fine.
examples_flagged: Gallery 825 serves as the exhibition space.

rules.message: Trailing present-participle clause that adds unsupported interpretation (Wikipedia 'superficial analyses'; Reinhart et al.: instruction-tuned LLMs use present participial clauses 2-5x the human rate).
rules.fix: Cut the -ing clause. If the interpretation matters, make it its own sentence and attribute it to a named source that actually says it.
examples_flagged: Sales rose 4%, highlighting the brand's enduring appeal.

rules.message: Vague attribution / weasel wording (Wikipedia WP:AIWEASEL). Also an unsubstantiated 'establishment claim' under FTC/ASA rules if used in ads.
rules.fix: Name the source and link it, or delete. Never invent the source. If the user supplied none, write the claim as the brand's own view or remove it.
rules.false_positive_notes: Downgrade to warning when a citation/link appears in the same sentence.
examples_flagged: Experts argue that the policy failed.
Studies show our app improves sleep.

rules.pattern: \b(?:(?:has been |was )?(?:featured|profiled|highlighted|covered) (?:in|by) (?:multiple|numerous|various|several|leading|prominent|major|other)\b|independent coverage|(?:maintains|has) an? (?:active|strong|robust) (?:social media|online|digital) presence|widely covered|garnered (?:significant |widespread )?(?:attention|acclaim|recognition))
rules.message: Canned emphasis on media coverage/notability (Wikipedia WP:AIATTR).
rules.fix: List the actual outlets with dates and links from the brief, or cut.
examples_flagged: She has been featured in numerous outlets.
The mall maintains an active social media presence.

rules.message: 'Not just X, but (also) Y' negative parallelism (Wikipedia WP:AIPARALLEL).
rules.fix: State Y directly. Keep the contrast only when a reader really holds belief X and you can show it is wrong.
examples_flagged: It's not just a tool, but a way of life.
examples_ok: It is a tool for cutting drywall.

rules.pattern: \b(?:it'?s|it is|this is|that'?s|that is|this isn'?t|it isn'?t|isn'?t)\s+(?:not\s+)?(?:just\s+|only\s+|merely\s+)?(?:about\s+)?[^.?!,;]{1,60}?(?:[,;:]|\s[—–-]\s|—|\.)\s*(?:it'?s|it is|this is|that'?s|but)\b
rules.message: 'It's not X, it's Y' / 'It isn't about X. It's about Y' reframing.
rules.fix: Say Y. Delete the straw-man X.
rules.false_positive_notes: Pattern is broad; confirm that the first clause contains a negation ('not', "n't") before flagging.
examples_flagged: It's not a product, it's a movement.
This isn't about speed. It's about trust.
examples_ok: It is a product for small teams.

rules.message: 'No X, no Y, just Z' formula.
rules.fix: Replace with one plain sentence stating Z and the evidence for it.
examples_flagged: No fluff, no filler, just results.
examples_ok: There was no filler in the report.

rules.threshold: flag when >=2 triads per 100 words or triads in 2 consecutive sentences (heuristic)
rules.message: Triadic lists (rule of three) used as a reflex (Wikipedia WP:RO3).
rules.fix: Keep a list of three only when there are exactly three real items. Otherwise use the one or two that matter, or the full list.
examples_flagged: It offers speed, clarity, and confidence.

rules.threshold: warning if >1 per 150 words or >1 per paragraph (heuristic)
rules.message: Em dash density. LLMs use em dashes more than non-professional human writers; a July 2026 study reported by The Economist found Claude used them more than professional writers (per Wikipedia).
rules.fix: Replace most with commas, colons, parentheses or full stops. Keep at most one em-dash pair per paragraph.

rules.pattern: (?:^|(?<=[.!?]\s))(?:In conclusion|In summary|To summari[sz]e|To sum up|Overall|All in all|Ultimately|In essence)\b,?
rules.message: Formulaic section/paragraph summary (Wikipedia historical indicator).
rules.fix: End on the last concrete point or the call to action; do not restate.

rules.message: 'Despite X, faces challenges...' + 'Future outlook' outline (Wikipedia WP:FACESCHALLENGES).
rules.fix: Name specific, sourced problems or drop the section.
examples_flagged: Despite its success, the company faces several challenges.
examples_ok: The company lost two contracts in 2024.

rules.message: Didactic 'it's important to note' disclaimers (Wikipedia historical indicator; Google: avoid placeholder phrases like 'please note').
rules.fix: Delete the frame; state the fact.
examples_flagged: It's important to note that fees apply.

rules.pattern: (?:^\s*(?:Certainly|Of course|Absolutely|Sure thing|Great question|Excellent question|What a great question)[!,.]|\bI hope this helps\b|\b(?:let me know|feel free to (?:ask|reach out)) if\b|\bWould you like me to\b|\bIs there anything else\b|\bHere(?:'s| is) (?:a|an|the|your) (?:revised|polished|updated|improved|detailed|refined|rewritten|draft)\b|\bAs an AI(?: language model)?\b|\bAs a large language model\b|\bYou'?re absolutely right\b)
rules.message: Chat-assistant correspondence left in deliverable text (Wikipedia 'collaborative communication').
rules.fix: Remove. Deliverables never address the requester or comment on the request.
examples_flagged: Certainly! Here is a revised version:
examples_ok: We hope the new schedule helps commuters.

rules.pattern: \b(?:as of my (?:last )?(?:knowledge|training) (?:update|cutoff|cut-off)|up to my last training|my knowledge cutoff|based on (?:the )?(?:available|provided) (?:information|sources|search results)|while specific details are (?:limited|scarce)|not widely (?:available|documented|disclosed|reported)|(?:maintains|keeps) a low profile|keeps (?:his|her|their) personal (?:life|details) private)\b
rules.message: Knowledge-cutoff disclaimer or speculation about gaps in sources (Wikipedia). These often precede invented 'likely' facts.
rules.fix: Delete. If a needed fact is missing, emit a visible [NEEDS SOURCE: ...] marker for the human instead of guessing.
examples_flagged: As of my last knowledge update, the CEO is Jane Doe.
examples_ok: The CEO is Jane Doe (company site, 2026).

rules.message: Unfilled template placeholder (Wikipedia 'phrasal templates and placeholder text').
rules.fix: Fill from the brief or stop and ask; never ship a placeholder.
rules.false_positive_notes: Intentional merge tags in email templates ({{first_name}}) should be whitelisted per channel.

rules.message: Internal citation/markup tokens leaked from chatbots (ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Perplexity) per Wikipedia.
rules.fix: Delete the artifact; re-check the claim it was attached to against a real source.

rules.message: Title Case heading. AI chatbots strongly tend to capitalise all main words (Wikipedia); Microsoft, Google, GOV.UK and Material use sentence case.
rules.fix: Use sentence case: capitalise the first word and proper nouns only (unless the house style is Chicago/AP-title or Apple menu/button).
rules.false_positive_notes: Headings made of proper nouns ('## New York Stock Exchange') -> keep a proper-noun allowlist.
examples_ok: ## Impact of technology on trade law

rules.threshold: warning if >1 bold span per 100 words in prose (heuristic)
rules.message: Mechanical boldface for emphasis (Wikipedia WP:AIBOLD; GOV.UK: do not use bold for emphasis).
rules.fix: Remove bold from running text; reserve bold for UI element names in instructions.

rules.message: Bullets that start with a bold inline header and colon (Wikipedia 'inline-header vertical lists').
rules.fix: Use prose, or plain bullets with a lead-in line (GOV.UK bullets rules).

rules.message: Emoji used as bullet/heading decoration (Wikipedia). Mailchimp: use emoji 'infrequently and deliberately'.
rules.fix: Remove from headings and bullets in professional copy; allow in social copy only if the brand voice permits.

rules.message: Mixed curly and straight quotes/apostrophes in one text (Wikipedia notes inconsistency as a sign; curly quotes alone prove nothing).
rules.fix: Normalise to the house choice (typographic curly quotes for print/web copy; straight in code).

rules.message: Vague 'associated with' instead of the stated relationship (Wikipedia WP:AICONNECT). Low precision alone.
rules.fix: State the relation: 'was CEO of', 'taught at', 'founded'.
rules.false_positive_notes: Legitimate in science ('X is associated with Y' = correlation). Only count in bios/company copy.
examples_flagged: He was associated with leadership of ExampleCorp.

rules.message: Sentence-initial transition used as filler; 'Additionally' is on Wikipedia's AI-vocabulary list (weak tell in isolation).
rules.fix: Delete, or use 'also'/'and' mid-sentence.

rules.message: Marketing verbs replacing neutral 'has' (Wikipedia WP:AINOCOPULA).
rules.fix: Use 'has' in descriptive copy unless 'offers' is literally an offer.
examples_flagged: The hotel boasts a rooftop pool.
examples_ok: The hotel has a rooftop pool.

rules.message: Sycophantic praise of the requester; sycophancy is a documented RLHF behaviour (Sharma et al.).
rules.fix: Remove. Critique on the merits.

rules.message: Quantitative claim. Must trace to the brief or a cited source.
rules.fix: Keep only if the number appears verbatim in the input facts or a cited source; else replace with [NEEDS SOURCE: metric] and do not estimate.
rules.false_positive_notes: Suppress when the same number exists in the input fact sheet (entity-diff check EN-FACT-005).

rules.message: Objective superlative/absolute claim needs documentary evidence (CAP 3.7; FTC reasonable-basis). Obvious puffery is tolerated; measurable superlatives are not.
rules.fix: Qualify with the source and scope ('fastest of 5 tools tested by X in 2026') or rewrite as a non-comparative benefit.

rules.message: Establishment claim: FTC expects at least the level of substantiation the ad claims ('tests prove', 'doctors recommend').
rules.fix: Cite the actual study/test (who, when, n, result) supplied by the client, or remove.
examples_ok: Designed to help you wind down.

rules.message: Customer quote/testimonial. FTC 16 CFR Part 465 (2024) bans fake testimonials, including AI-generated ones and ones from people who do not exist.
rules.fix: Use only quotes supplied verbatim by the client with a real, consenting source; otherwise use a clearly marked [TESTIMONIAL NEEDED] slot.
examples_flagged: “This app changed my life.” — Sarah K., Marketing Manager
examples_ok: Our customers include Acme (case study linked).

rules.pattern: (algorithmic: extract numbers, dates, money, percentages, proper nouns, URLs, quotes from output; diff against input brief + cited sources)
rules.message: Any specific fact (name, number, date, award, customer, study) that is not present in the brief or an attached source is presumed invented.
rules.fix: Remove or replace with a [NEEDS SOURCE] marker; list all such items in the QA report to the human.

rules.message: DOI/ISBN present: Wikipedia lists invalid DOIs/ISBNs and DOIs leading to unrelated papers as AI signs.
rules.fix: Resolve every DOI (doi.org) and validate ISBN checksums; confirm title/author match the claim.

rules.threshold: warning >25 words; error >40 words (the 40 is a heuristic)
rules.message: GOV.UK: check sentences over 25 words; plainlanguage: one idea per sentence.
rules.fix: Split at the conjunction or move conditions into their own sentence.

rules.message: plainlanguage.gov: paragraphs of no more than 150 words in 3-8 sentences; never longer than 250.
rules.fix: Split by topic; add a heading if needed.

rules.message: Passive construction (plainlanguage, GOV.UK, Mailchimp, Google all prefer active voice).
rules.fix: Name the actor: 'The form must be completed' -> 'You must complete the form'.
rules.false_positive_notes: Adjectival participles ('is interested', 'is based in') cause false positives; count density, not single hits.
examples_flagged: The form must be completed by you.

rules.message: Hidden verb / nominalisation (plainlanguage 'avoid hidden verbs'; GOV.UK: -ion/-ment words lengthen sentences).
rules.fix: 'conduct an analysis' -> 'analyse'; 'make a decision' -> 'decide'; 'provide assistance' -> 'help'.
examples_flagged: We conducted an analysis of costs.

rules.pattern: \b(?:at this point in time|due to the fact that|at the present time|in accordance with|for the purpose of|has the ability to|in the event that|in the amount of|in the event of|with regard to|in order that|subsequent to|approximately|subsequently|in regard to|utilization|in order to|methodology|a number of|demonstrate|facilitate|promulgate|assistance|sufficient|is able to|additional|implement|endeavour|ascertain|terminate|commence|prior to|numerous|endeavor|purchase|initiate|utilize|utilise|assist)\b
rules.message: Formal word where a common one works (plainlanguage 'dirty dozen' and simple-words table; GOV.UK clear language).
rules.fix: Replace per map: utilize -> use; utilise -> use; utilization -> use; facilitate -> help, ease (or say how); commence -> begin, start; implement -> carry out, start; in accordance with -> under, per, following; in order to -> to; in order that -> so; in the event of -> if; in the event that -> if; in the amount of -> for; promulgate -> issue, publish; assist -> help; assistance -> help; prior to -> before; subsequent to -> after; subsequently -> later, then; numerous -> many; sufficient -> enough; methodology -> method; endeavor -> try; endeavour -> try; ascertain -> find out; approximately -> about; purchase -> buy; due to the fact that -> because; at this point in time -> now; at the present time -> now; a number of -> some; with regard to -> about; in regard to -> about; for the purpose of -> to, for; is able to -> can; has the ability to -> can; initiate -> start; terminate -> end; demonstrate -> show; additional -> more, extra
examples_flagged: We utilize AI in order to help.

rules.message: 'Shall' is ambiguous; use 'must' for requirements (plainlanguage; GOV.UK: use 'must' for legal requirements).
rules.fix: Use 'must' / 'must not'.
rules.false_positive_notes: Quoted legal text must stay verbatim.
examples_flagged: The user shall submit the form.

rules.message: Double negative (plainlanguage 'use positive language').
rules.fix: 'no fewer than' -> 'at least'; 'is not ... unless' -> 'is ... only if'.

rules.message: Slashes are ambiguous (plainlanguage 'don't use slashes'; GOV.UK: avoid document(s)).
rules.fix: 'a and/or b' -> 'a or b or both'; pick one term.
rules.false_positive_notes: Skip URLs, dates, fractions, units (km/h), code.
examples_ok: Bring your ID or passport, or both.

rules.pattern: \b(?:please note|kindly note|note that|at this time|be advised|it should be noted)\b
rules.message: Placeholder phrases (Google: avoid 'please note', 'at this time'; GOV.UK: usually no need for 'please'/'please note').
rules.fix: Delete the phrase.
examples_flagged: Please note that the office is closed.

rules.message: Google: avoid 'simply', 'It's easy', 'quickly' in instructions (condescending if the reader struggles).
rules.fix: Delete, or give the actual time/steps.

rules.threshold: error on '!!'; warning if >1 per 300 words or any in error/alert copy
rules.message: Mailchimp: exclamation points sparingly, never more than one at a time, never in failure messages; Google: avoid exclamation marks.
rules.fix: Remove; let the fact carry the energy.

rules.message: Microsoft: avoid weak phrasing like 'there is/are/were'.
rules.fix: Start with the real subject and verb.
examples_flagged: There are three ways to pay.

rules.threshold: flag first occurrence when no '(ABBR)' or 'ABBR (' expansion exists earlier and ABBR not in allowlist
rules.message: First use of an uncommon abbreviation without expansion (GOV.UK, plainlanguage, Mailchimp).
rules.fix: Expand on first use: 'Personal Independence Payment (PIP)'. Skip universally known ones (BBC, API, HTML).
examples_ok: Submit the data protection impact assessment (DPIA).

rules.message: GOV.UK 'words to avoid' and metaphors.
rules.fix: going forward -> from now on/in the future; drive -> create/cause/encourage; deliver -> make/create/provide; tackle -> stop/solve/deal with.
examples_flagged: Going forward, we will drive growth.
examples_ok: From now on, we will grow sales by...

rules.message: List of 3+ without serial comma. Required by Chicago (CMOS 6.19), Microsoft, Google, Mailchimp; AP uses it only to avoid ambiguity.
rules.fix: Profile Chicago/Microsoft/Google/Mailchimp: add the comma before and/or. Profile AP: leave off in simple series.

rules.message: Spaced em dash or hyphen-as-dash. Chicago, Microsoft ('Don't be spacey') and Mailchimp use closed em dashes; AP spaces them. Wikipedia notes spaced em dashes are typical of AI output.
rules.fix: Profile Chicago/Microsoft/Mailchimp: word—word. Profile AP: word — word. Better: fewer dashes (EN-AI-031).

rules.message: Numeral for one to nine in body text. AP and Microsoft spell out zero/one-nine; Chicago spells out zero-one hundred in nontechnical text (CMOS 9.2); GOV.UK uses numerals for everything except 'one' in phrases.
rules.fix: Apply profile: AP/Microsoft -> words for 1-9 (except ages, %, measurements, times, steps); Chicago -> words to 100; GOV.UK -> numerals.

rules.message: Do not start a sentence with a numeral (Microsoft, GOV.UK, Mailchimp).
rules.fix: Spell it out ('Thirty-four') or add a modifier ('More than 10 apps...').
rules.false_positive_notes: List items may start with numerals (Microsoft).

rules.message: All-numeric dates are ambiguous across locales (Microsoft global tip).
rules.fix: Spell the month: en-US 'June 12, 2017'; en-GB/GOV.UK '12 June 2017' (no comma).

rules.message: GOV.UK: use 'to' in ranges, not hyphens or dashes (except tables). Microsoft: 'from...through', en dash only for pages/space-limited UI.
GOV.UK and Mailchimp: use 'and', not '&', except in brand/company names.
rules.fix: Replace with 'and'.
rules.false_positive_notes: Brand names (AT&T, M&S, H&M) and code.

rules.message: Microsoft: no period or colon at the end of titles and headings.
rules.fix: Remove the final period/colon.

rules.message: Microsoft: one space after periods, question marks and colons.
rules.fix: Use one space.

rules.pattern: \[(?:click here|here|read more|more|this link|learn more|link)\]\(|]*>\s*(?:click here|here|read more|more)\s*
rules.message: Mailchimp: never 'Click here'; Google: descriptive link text.
rules.fix: Link the words that describe the destination.

rules.message: GOV.UK: do not use block capitals for large amounts of text; read as shouting.
rules.fix: Use sentence case.
examples_flagged: DO NOT USE BLOCK CAPITALS HERE
examples_ok: Do not use block capitals here

rules.message: GOV.UK: avoid eg/ie/etc (screen readers read 'eg' as 'egg').
rules.fix: Use 'for example', 'such as', 'that is', or finish the list.

rules.message: GOV.UK avoids negative and complex contractions. (Microsoft and Mailchimp encourage contractions: rule applies only to GOV.UK profile.)
rules.fix: GOV.UK profile: 'cannot', 'do not'.

rules.pattern: (document check: both variants of a spelling family present, see US_UK_FAMILIES)
rules.message: Mixed US and UK spelling in one text.
rules.fix: Pick en-US or en-GB from the brief and normalise every family. For en-GB with Oxford spelling, -ize is legitimate (OED) but GOV.UK requires -ise.

rules.message: FRE = 206.835 - 1.015*(words/sentences) - 84.6*(syllables/words). 60-70 = 'plain English' (8th-9th grade).
rules.fix: Consumer copy target FRE >= 60; warn < 50; error < 30 (thresholds are heuristics anchored on Flesch's bands).

rules.message: FKGL = 0.39*(words/sentences) + 11.8*(syllables/words) - 15.59.
rules.fix: General public/health: <= 8 (IOM 2015 via NCI); insurance precedent: <= 9 (Pennsylvania); B2B/technical: <= 12 (heuristic). Report, do not game (short words alone do not make text clear).
